For Chord Types: m7b5

Locrian #2, the sixth mode of melodic minor, is constructed just as its name suggests-like the Locrian mode (seventh mode of the major scale), but with a raised 2nd degree. Like the Locrian mode, its chief application is over m7>5 chords.

Aitered Scale (Super Locrian)

(Seventh made of melodic minor)

For Chord Types: Altered Dom? (functioning) Fig. 6

The altered scale-or Super Locrian-is the seventh mode of the melodic minor scale. The altered scale is similar in construc- tion to the Locrian mode, but whereas the latter contains a perfect 4th, the altered scale has a diminished 4th, which is enhar- monic to a major 3rd degree. This results in the presence of both a minor 3rd and a major 3rd, but many players view the formula as 1-»9-#9-3-5-45-57. As you can see, all possible alterations are present: 9, #9, b5, and #5. Combined with its major 3rd and b7th degrees, this makes the altered scale an ideal choice for soloing over the functioning altered dominant chords in minor key chord progressions.
